question: A project lead is told she cannot send any more messages for several hours, and the block applies even in a brand-new empty chat. Which limit has she reached?
options: A) A length limit, which governs how much information a single chat can work with at one time.
B) A knowledge limit, which governs how many documents a single project workspace is able to store.
C) An artifact limit, which governs how many separate documents Claude can produce within one session.
D) A usage limit, which governs how much she can interact with Claude over a given period of time.
correct_answers: D) A usage limit, which governs how much she can interact with Claude over a given period of time.
explanations: Incorrect. A length limit is confined to one conversation's context window; starting a fresh chat would clear it immediately.
Incorrect. A cap on stored documents would not stop her sending messages in an unrelated new chat.
Incorrect. There is no such block on messaging, and artifacts are an output format rather than a messaging quota.
Correct. Usage limits control how much you can interact with Claude across a time period, so they follow you into every chat, including a new one.
